the plant grows in the west, which makes it slightly adapted to drier conditions. the internet says it's not a coastal plant so that rules out a wet climate. depending on where you are, the plant appears to bloom late spring. the internet also says it prefers quick draining soil and grows from mid to high elevations. it can have deep roots which evidently helps with finding water, and withstanding fires. it's possible that it may have a few big roots shooting straight down.

with this information i would follow this plan - cut into the soil around the plant with your shovel now, creating a circle well inside the drip line. it will have all winter to heal and form tiny new roots. depending on where you live i would either a) dig it up early spring before it blooms, (soil conditions may be to cold/frozen etc.) or b) wait till after it blooms. make sure you dig slightly outside of the circle you dug before so you get the new formed roots. water it heavy the night before you dig so that its thirst is satiated. either way, trim back the tips so that no blooms or seed heads form.
